summary: Moon Base: Mission on Foot is a bilingual, browser-based survival game designed for children ages 7–12. Players lead a seven-day mission on the Moon or Mars, explore a changing landscape, collect oxygen, power, water, and science samples, and return to base before time or protection runs out. Each choice affects crew health, energy, shielding, crops, and the next day’s plan. The game turns space science into hands-on decisions about solar storms, radiation, reduced gravity, and growing food in a greenhouse. Historical solar-event examples are based on NASA DONKI, while the game can query public NASA and OSDR resources when an internet connection is available. Simulated countdowns and damage are identified as gameplay simplifications, not real-time forecasts or personal radiation measurements. The project makes planetary exploration approachable, encourages scientific curiosity, and helps young learners imagine themselves as future explorers.
details:
Moon Base: Mission on Foot is a bilingual, browser-based educational survival game for children ages 7–12. Players choose the Moon or Mars and lead a seven-day expedition. They explore a procedurally generated landscape, collect oxygen, power, water, and science samples, manage health and shielding, care for greenhouse crops, and return to base before time runs out or a storm creates danger. Each day’s report shows the consequences of choices and lets players upgrade the habitat.

The game teaches resource management, solar storms, radiation, gravity, and food production through hands-on play. Its intended impact is to make space science approachable and spark curiosity about future exploration.

It was built with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, using the Canvas 2D API for graphics, Web Audio API for synthesized sound, and localStorage to save progress. The game can query public NASA DONKI space-weather data and NASA OSDR/RadLab resources when connected. It runs in a browser, supports touch and keyboard controls, and does not require installation.

The creative approach combines a survival loop with real historical solar events while clearly labeling damage and countdowns as simplified game mechanics, not real-time forecasts or suit measurements. The team considered age-appropriate language, bilingual access, mobile performance, and scientific accuracy.
